content:
I play-tested v18 locally with the supplied referee against all three bosses in both player seats. Both games completed, and the color swap and combined scores matched the rules.

One reproducible onboarding issue: the Python starter in your forum announcement parses all five header fields with map(int, input().split()), but side is now B or O. It crashes before the first move with ValueError. Keeping side as a string fixes it; I verified that the corrected example completes both games. Could you update the forum snippet?

One optional addition: a few language-independent scoring examples—board positions with expected Blue/Orange totals—would help bot authors validate their evaluators before tuning search. Cases where the nearest distance layer is tied and a farther layer decides ownership would be especially useful. The Java tests already cover this; providing a few plain-text fixtures would make those checks easy to reuse in other languages.

I haven't read the statement in detail or done any play-testing yet. My feedback below is focused primarily on the high-level presentation and structure of the statement.

* Here's a link to a statement for your reference: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1516179aa763a6302dbdfa2c8676688ed085c3 (click "Test in ide").

* The statement contains several long paragraphs. Consider breaking the content into smaller subsections and using bullet points where appropriate to make it easier to scan and understand.

* Consider adding diagrams or images to illustrate the concepts.

* Use <var> and <const> tags throughout the statement, where appropriate, to make variable names and constants easily identifiable.

* Define variables. For example, in the Territory Scoring section, `dr` and `dc` are used without being defined.

* Please add separate sections for "Victory Conditions" and "Defeat Conditions".

* Game input: The introductory paragraph "The input describes…" appears unnecessary and can be removed.

* Input / Output headings: Please append "per game turn" to both headings.

* Input Line 1: Please specify that the five integers are space-separated.

* Next line: Please specify that `legalActionCount` is an integer, and explain what it represents.

* Next legalActionCount: Please specify that each legal action index is an integer.

* Output: The formulas "action / 16" and "action % 16" shouldn't be included in the output description. The meaning of the action index and its relationship to board positions should instead be defined in the Rules section. Where possible, use plain language rather than formulas.

* Constraints: Please split the constraints into individual points, with one constraint per line.

* Consider adding a link to the referee code.

* If the game concept is based on an existing game or another source, please acknowledge and credit the original creator or source.

* Viewer: Please add an opening animation when the puzzle viewer is launched.

* Please upload a cover picture for the puzzle.

Thanks.
Thank you. The rules are my own design.

Thanks again for your detailed feedback! I've updated the statement, added rule diagrams and a cover, and included an opening replay with live territory visualization. The contribution is now ready for review. If you have time, I'd really appreciate another look and any further feedback.
Would you mind switching the status of the puzzle to WIP to give more time for reviewers to comment on it? Thank you.

I've taken a more detailed look at the statement, although I haven't done any play-testing yet. Below are my comments on the updated statement. General * Is there any compelling reason to run both games in parallel? It seems that they could be played sequentially, one after the other, without significantly affecting the gameplay (except for access to a much earlier result of the first completed game). As a comparison, you may want to look at Shobu, which also has two rounds in which players switch colours. However, the rounds are played sequentially rather than in parallel. Link to Shobu: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/156996d51cd504680231438ef0402fb9e42507 * Changing to playing one game at a time would also simplify some of the rules and the overall game flow. * The text in the viewer is currently very small. Although fullscreen mode allows players to magnify the display, having only one board displayed at a time would free up more space for other elements, such as the game number and players' names, allowing these to be displayed more prominently. Viewer * Please increase the font size wherever possible, including the row and column labels. * Players' names are missing. Please add them to the viewer. * If space permits, consider displaying players' icons as well. Victory Conditions & Defeat Conditions * Please reformat these sections using the standard presentation format: • a teal background with trophy icon for Victory Conditions, and • a red background with skull for Defeat Conditions. You may refer to the linked statement in my first comment for the required HTML code. Draw Conditions * Since there isn't a standard format for this section, feel free to come up with a design that aligns with the Victory Conditions and Defeat Conditions sections. Input per game turn * No change is necessary, but I find it slightly inconsistent that `side` uses 1 and 2, whereas the board representation uses B and W for the two colours. 1 and 2 may be replaced with B and W for `side`, but it's totally up to you. Output per game turn * Please change "Output one line containing" to "One line:". Constraints * Please remove the 2nd and 3rd constraints. * Please remove the constraint beginning with "A final territory". * Reason for removal: The four constraints are largely redundant. Credits and Referee Source * We don't usually link to the Game Engine (which should actually be called the SDK) or the contribution page. Please remove both links. Leagues * Please add a "Leagues" section explaining that the game has three leagues, with the league bosses being the only difference between them. The game rules are identical across all three leagues. I'll carry out play-testing once the contribution is closer to its final form. Thanks.
Thanks. It's late night here. I'll fix these tomorrow. Once done, I'll reply.
Feel free to give it a try.

The viewer is a substantial improvement over the previous version. Good job.

Rules
* The final point ("Each input describes … for each game.") in the "A match contains two games" section is now redundant and can be removed.

Input per game turn
* Please change "fields" to "values" (twice).

* Please add this sentence before the bullet-point list: "They are all integers except for <var>side</var>."

Credits and Referee Source
* The current link to the referee code also provides access to the bosses' code, which might not be ideal. If possible, please provide a link to the referee code only.

Stub
* Line 2: Please replace "string" with "word(1)", as using "string" causes a syntax error.

Viewer
* The final score summary screen is missing. Please use SDK's endScreenModule (see section 4 of the documentation) to implement it.

Thanks.
Thank you for all the previous updates. I don't have further comments at this moment.
Thank you for all the advice. Why not try to defeat my bosses😁.
